shortlist.label: Congestive heart failure
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and symptoms of edema

shortlist.label: Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and global hypokinesis

shortlist.label: Nephrotic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, which could be related to nephrotic syndrome

shortlist.label: Lymphedema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has edema in the lower extremities, which could be related to lymphedema

shortlist.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has alternating QRS complex morphologies and delta wave present in QRS complex B, suggestive of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's history of NYHA stage III heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, and elevated brain natriuretic peptide level are consistent with congestive heart failure.

rejected.label: Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a reduced ejection fraction, cardiomyopathy is a broader term and the patient's presentation is more consistent with the specific diagnosis of congestive heart failure.

rejected.label: Nephrotic syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of significant proteinuria or other signs of nephrotic syndrome.

rejected.label: Lymphedema
rejected.why: The patient's edema is more likely related to his heart failure than a primary lymphatic disorder.

rejected.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has an abnormal ECG with delta waves, his presentation is not consistent with the typical symptoms of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, such as paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia.
